To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) there is a differential rate of improvement for different symptom dimensions, (2) the improvement rate of each of these symptom dimensions is different from the others, (3) the rate of improvement for each symptom dimension is different from the other symptom dimensions and (4) the rate of change of one symptom dimension is different than the rate of change for the others.
the high serum level group improved more than the low level group on a symptom subscale of the Hopkins Symptom Check-list 90.
the rate of symptom change differed for different symptom clusters and that the Psychotic symptom subscale of the SCL-90-R was a good predictor of treatment outcome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the differential improvement of different symptoms of anxiety in patients treated for panic disorder and agoraphobia using a combination of pharmacotherapy and in vivo exposure therapy.
the development of a behavioral treatment for agoraphobia that is as efficacious and as rapid in its onset of action as the pharmacological treatments.
the differential rates of change of the various symptoms of agoraphobic subjects as they undergo a combined pharmacological and exposure treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rate of change of different subscales of the SCL-90-R is different for different symptoms.
in vivo exposure treatment for agoraphobia is a time limited treatment.

the rate of change for the different symptom subscales differed throughout the course of treatment, that there were no differences between the high and low serum levels of imipramines on the rate of improvement of the different symptom scales and finally that the Psychoticism scale was the only scale that could discriminate the responsive vs nonresponsive subjects after the first week of treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in vivo exposure therapy is effective in treating agoraphobia, that the high and low serum imipramine groups are equally responsive to treatment, that the rate of change of different symptom subscales is not uniform throughout treatment and that the Psychoticism symptom subscale may be useful in differentiating responsive vs nonresponsive agoraphobics.
in vivo exposure therapy is effective for the treatment of agorapobia.
the rate of response of different symptoms to combined pharmacological and in vivo exposure therapy for agoraphobia is dependent upon the type of symptom.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the different rates of improvement of the different symptom subscales are consistent with the hypothesis that the symptoms of agoraphobic patients are not unitary in origin.
different symptoms respond at different rates to treatment.
the rate of symptom improvement is not uniform across all symptoms.
